title: “We should be more ambitious with the software we build”
date_basis: Publisher RSS entry at https://danluu.com/atom.xml: pubDate Sat, 24 Oct 2026 00:00:00 +0000; entry link and guid match the essay. The endpoint contains RSS XML, despite its filename.
summary: Argues that AI expands feasible software projects, not merely task speed; pairs practical examples with verification constraints and Kreinin's caution about excessive ambition.
limitations: Selected practitioner accounts, not a controlled effect. The author discloses limited benchmarking. Personal-tool usability does not establish production readiness; quoted discussion is not a separate study. Model, speed and cost claims are not independently reproduced here.

verification.basis: Full essay, appendices, counterargument and caveats inspected; exact publication date matched in publisher RSS using a structured XML parser. Two linked PostgreSQL reports and their replies were inspected separately, without executing their reproducers.

title: Re: BUG #19597: getQuadrant: impossible case is reachable
date_basis: Official PostgreSQL mailing-list archive: message date and Message-ID.
summary: Tiwari reports reproducing Malis's SP-GiST numerical-boundary bug on upstream master and proposes a patch. This supports the existence of a concrete validation outcome, not a general AI effect.
limitations: We read the messages but did not run the reproducer, inspect the attachment or establish a merged fix. Neither message isolates AI's causal contribution or validates pgrust's overall compatibility, performance or production readiness.

verification.basis: Official archive metadata, original report and full reply inspected; quoted report distinguished from the reply author's reproduction statement. No code executed.

title: Re: BUG #19594: to_char/jsonpath format cache serves a format tree parsed in the wrong strict-mode
date_basis: Official PostgreSQL mailing-list archive: message date and Message-ID.
summary: Rachitskiy agrees with Malis's cache-mode analysis, supplies a patch and regression test, and requests review. This corroborates a specific report reaching technical follow-up.
limitations: A proposed patch is not proof of a merged or deployed fix. Attachments were not independently evaluated. The discussion does not identify a counterfactual without AI or establish overall project quality.

verification.basis: Official archive metadata, original report and full reply inspected; proposed patch and regression test noted from the reply, not independently run or reviewed.

title: Re: [PATCH] docs: remove Assisted-by references
date_basis: Message Date header displayed in local Chrome: 13 October 2026, 13:45:09 -0700. Not the archive update date.
summary: Torvalds opposes categorical tool bans and argues that contributors should understand their changes regardless of the tools used. His compiler and editor analogies defend tool use; they do not measure AI reliability or productivity.
limitations: A maintainer's normative position in a contested thread, not an experiment, representative survey or proof of a merged policy change. Understanding is asserted as an expectation, not independently measured.

verification.basis: Full rendered message, author, Date header and quoted parent context inspected in the user's existing local Chrome tab.

title: Re: [PATCH] docs: remove Assisted-by references
date_basis: Message Date header displayed in local Chrome: 13 October 2026, 22:16:28 +0200.
summary: Pinchart argues that explicit expectations retain value despite imperfect enforcement and questions AI-written commit explanations. The quoted exchange proposes human-written rationale as a way to discourage submissions that their senders do not understand.
limitations: Does not establish that manual writing guarantees understanding or that generated prose can be reliably detected. References to Mesa are the participant's comparison, not an independently checked Mesa-policy citation.

verification.basis: Full rendered message, metadata and quoted Cook/Pinchart exchange inspected in local Chrome; distinguishes the author's reply from quoted text.

title: Re: [PATCH] docs: remove Assisted-by references
date_basis: Message Date header displayed in local Chrome: 14 October 2026, 11:47:46 -0700.
summary: Cook separates an origin declaration from evidence of understanding. He describes useful AI drafting, review-volume constraints, testing and contributor trust as distinct considerations; a binary tool tag does not establish patch quality.
limitations: Practitioner self-report and policy reasoning, not measured improvement. Reported review mechanisms and Sashiko features were not independently evaluated. Trust filters can have participation costs; their effectiveness is not established here.

verification.basis: Full rendered follow-up, metadata, review criteria and closing discussion inspected in local Chrome; linked bot implementation not evaluated.

title: [PATCH v2] docs: remove Assisted-by references
date_basis: Indiana University archive displays the 13 October 2026 message; no inference from its crawl date.
container_title: Linux Kernel Mailing List (Indiana University archive)
summary: The revised proposal motivates dropping the structured Assisted-by trailer through weak disclosure coverage, while retaining transparency and human responsibility. It reports strong but non-unanimous summit support, not a representative vote.
limitations: Proposal and author-reported rationale, not proof of merge or an independently audited usage census. Tagged-commit share does not estimate true AI adoption. The v1 and v2 patches are versions of one proposal.

verification.basis: Author-attributed v2 message, rationale and diff inspected in the public university archive; v1 inspected separately. Primary lore archive was access-blocked.

title: Linux Kernel Drops AI Tag Requirement, Uses Meta AI For Code Reviews
date_basis: Publisher byline and publication date on the inspected article.
summary: Connects tag removal with AI-assisted review and offers a skeptical governance interpretation. Its definite headline is stronger than the implementation status established by this intake.
limitations: Not independent effectiveness evidence. The broad assertion about most open-source projects is unsupported by this article and is not adopted; neither are bot-performance claims. No representative analysis of reader comments was conducted.

verification.basis: Article body, byline, date and selected outbound primary-source links inspected; reader comments not treated as surveyed opinion.
